sentences.text: Mr. H.B. Agrawal, learned Senior Advocate along with Ms. A. Sndhya Rao, learned counsel for the appellant.
Mr. Anand Gupta, learned Dy. GA for the State.
Heard on the application for amendment.

Learned counsel for the applicant submits that due to a bona fide mistake, instead of filing an appeal under Section 76(1) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, the present matter has been filed as a Criminal Miscellaneous Petition under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C.
It is further submitted that the matter was initially presented as a Criminal Appeal; however, on account of confusion, it was corrected and placed as a CRMP.

It is, therefore, prayed that the cause title be permitted to be corrected and necessary amendments be incorporated in the petition so as to treat the same as an appeal under Section 76(1) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

Considering the reasons assigned in the application and the submission made by learned counsel,
the prayer for amendment appears to be bona fide and procedural in nature.
Accordingly, the petitioner is permitted to carry out necessary amendment in the cause title and relevant pleadings and also filed the amended memo of appeal within a period of seven days.

Upon such amendment being carried out, the Registry is directed to register the matter as an appeal under Section 76(1) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and place the same before the appropriate Bench as per roster.
